// What to look for
//
// #2191 reports an ASSERT. Compiler Explorer runs Release builds of DXC, where
// asserts are compiled out (include/llvm/llvm_assert/assert.h: `#ifdef NDEBUG
// #define assert(_Expression) ((void)0)`), so every DXC pane below compiles this
// cleanly. That clean compile is NOT evidence the bug is gone.
//
// On a Debug build of main (1.9.0.15422, eff900d54) the same input dies with
//   Internal compiler error: LLVM Assert          (exit 0xE0000001)
//   assert(MaybeODRUseExprs.empty() && "Leftover expressions for odr-use checking")
//   tools/clang/lib/Sema/SemaDecl.cpp(11156), in clang::Sema::ActOnFinishFunctionBody
//
// So the two things worth reading here are:
//
//   1. DXC panes: the compile SUCCEEDS and the metadata says NumThreads=(8,8,1)
//      (look for `!{i32 8, i32 8, i32 1}`, or NumThreads in the comment header).
//      The `static const uint` was resolved correctly -- shipping DXC accepts
//      this construct and always has, back to v1.4.1907. Release users are
//      unaffected; the defect is confined to assert-enabled builds.
//
//   2. Clang (assertions trunk): CE has no assertions-enabled DXC, but it does
//      carry an assertions build of the successor HLSL front end. That pane is
//      the closest available answer to "does an assert-enabled compiler still
//      trip on this?"
//
// The empty function body is load-bearing, not laziness: any full expression in
// the body drains the bookkeeping the assert checks, and the assert stops firing.
